name: semantic-crosscheck
description: Cross-layer verification for an ontology plus semantic layer on PostgreSQL 17, for Codex and Claude Code.

interface.shortDescription: Prove that a PostgreSQL closure, SHACL rules, OWL reasoning and a Cube model agree.
interface.longDescription: Release v0.15.0: cross-check PostgreSQL 17 closures, SQL/SHACL rules, OWL/HermiT and Cube against independently authored gold SQL. Optional authored expectation cases can pin a local business-definition file by SHA-256; missing, changed, blocked or unavailable source evidence stops fixture cases before DB access and completion drift demotes affected passes. The okf diagnostic exports explicitly selected contract metadata or previews the closed SXC OKF 0.2 profile without SQL, source text, rows, credentials, runtime receipts or import application. Standalone knowledge-evolution exercises five fixed source transitions and 26 independent synthetic contracts through actual input/source/report APIs, with no DB, engine or model execution. Source currency, profile completion and synthetic replay never grant semantic approval or operational PASS. Existing report requirements and dependency pins remain unchanged. Rerun operational stages after upgrading.
defaultPrompt: Use semantic-crosscheck to run the synthetic demo end to end.
Use semantic-crosscheck to verify my crosscheck.toml against PostgreSQL and explain what is not proven.
